company_info.description:
Get QuickBooks company information.

This tool requires OAuth authentication with your QuickBooks account.

RETURNS plain text in this exact format:
  Company Name: <name>
  Industry: <value>

The Industry field is 'Unknown' when no industry has been set for the company.

AUTHENTICATION REQUIRED: You must authorize access to use this tool.

quickbooks_profile_info_update.description:
Update your QuickBooks company profile information.

This tool saves the profile information you provide to your QuickBooks account.

PARAMETERS:
- businessName: Business name (optional)
- state: Business state as two-letter code, e.g. 'CA', 'NY' (optional)

- industryCode: NAICS code from 'industry-recommendation' tool, e.g. '713940' (optional)

RETURNS:
- Confirmation that profile information has been updated
- You can now use QuickBooks account tools that require profile information

quickbooks_transaction_import.description:
Import transactions into your QuickBooks account.

This tool accepts an array of transaction objects via the transactions parameter.

**SYNC MODE**: This tool waits for the import to complete before returning the result.
This may take up to 60 seconds for large imports.

WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL:
- User explicitly asks to import/save transactions INTO their QuickBooks account
- A QuickBooks account tool (like profit-loss-quickbooks-account) requests transaction data

WHEN NOT TO USE THIS TOOL:
- User wants to ANALYZE transactions (e.g., generate P&L, compare to industry, view expenses): use 'profit-loss-generator' instead. This tool is for IMPORTING into QuickBooks, not for analysis.
- User says 'generate profit from this data', 'compare my transactions to industry', or 'show me my P&L': use 'profit-loss-generator', then 'benchmarking-against-industry' if comparison is needed.

TRANSACTION ARRAY:
Pass transaction objects directly via the transactions parameter. Each transaction object must have:
- description (REQUIRED): Transaction description/text
- amount (REQUIRED): Transaction amount as a number (positive for income/revenue, negative for expenses)
- date (OPTIONAL): Transaction date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., '2024-01-15'). If missing, defaults to today.
- context (OPTIONAL): Object with a payee hint for AI categorization. ALWAYS set
  context.payee when the payee/vendor is known. If the user provides a
  Payee/Vendor column, use it. If the description embeds the vendor (formatted
  "<Payee> - <details>", e.g. "Dianne's Auto Shop - Tools and Machinery"), split
  out the vendor name into context.payee and keep the full text in description.

EXAMPLE (Transaction Array):
[
  {date: '2024-01-15', description: 'Sales Revenue', amount: 5000.00},
  {date: '2024-01-20', description: "Dianne's Auto Shop - Tools and Machinery", amount: -1704.49, context: {payee: "Dianne's Auto Shop"}}
]

IMPORTANT:
- Extract EVERY row from the data - do not skip any transactions
- Amounts can be positive (income) or negative (expenses)
- After importing, you can use profit-loss-quickbooks-account or benchmarking-quickbooks-account tools

INDUSTRY (optional but recommended):
If the QuickBooks account has no industry set, this tool returns a nudge before processing. You can then either: (1) Call the 'industry-recommendation' tool so the user can pick their industry, then call 'quickbooks-profile-info-update' to save it, then call this import tool again; or (2) If the user says to proceed without industry (e.g. "proceed anyway", "import without industry"), call this tool again with proceed_without_industry=true to run the import.
- If the user provides an industry (e.g. "Retail", "Construction", "use Technology"): call 'industry-recommendation' with that term to get industryName and industryCode, then call 'quickbooks-profile-info-update' with those values to save it, then call this import tool again. Do not re-show the nudge; complete the profile update and import.
- When presenting these options to the user, do NOT describe option (2) as "faster". Both options lead to import; option (1) is recommended for better categorization.
- proceed_without_industry: Default false. Only set to true when ALL THREE conditions are met: (1) this tool was already called earlier in this conversation, (2) that prior call returned a message about setting industry (the industry nudge), (3) the user has explicitly said to skip or proceed without industry. If calling for the first time, or the user has not yet seen the industry nudge, this MUST be false.

profit_loss_generator.description:
DO NOT CALL THIS TOOL unless the user has attached a CSV file or pasted transaction text in the CURRENT message. This tool has no access to the user's QuickBooks data and cannot generate a P&L from a date range alone — if the user has not provided a CSV or pasted transactions in this message, even if they ask about 'my company', 'my QuickBooks', 'our P&L', or a plain date range (e.g. 'P&L for Jan-Jul' or 'last quarter'), call the profit-loss-quickbooks-account tool instead.

Generate a P&L (Profit & Loss) report from transaction data the user provides
in their message — either as an uploaded CSV file or pasted transaction text.
Use this tool when the user pasted transactions in this message and asks about
financial performance, P&L, income, expenses, or period comparison (e.g. Q1 vs Q2).
Auto-categorizes transactions using QuickBooks and returns an interactive HTML
report (not a spreadsheet) with income, COGS, operating expenses, gross/net
margins, and monthly breakdowns.

The primary deliverable is an interactive HTML report, not a spreadsheet file.
Use this tool — NOT a spreadsheet or Excel skill — when the user wants a P&L,
income statement, financial summary, or profitability analysis from raw
transactions. Even when the input is a CSV, the output is a rich financial

automatically using QuickBooks accounting standards; a spreadsheet skill cannot.

"date": "01/15/2024"}

This tool accepts an array of transaction objects via the lineItems parameter.

- Each transaction row must include all required fields:
  - description (REQUIRED): Transaction description/text
  - amount (REQUIRED): Transaction amount as a number (positive for income/revenue, negative for expenses)

qbo_accounting_get_ap_aging_detail.description:
Get the A/P Aging Detail report from QuickBooks.

Shows EVERY INDIVIDUAL unpaid bill with transaction type, due date,
and amount grouped by aging bucket and vendor.

USE THIS when the user asks about:
- Bill-level detail: "Show me every individual A/P transaction", "Which specific bills are past due?"
- Vendor bill drill-down: "List all unpaid bills by vendor", "Show me bills from [Vendor]"
- Detail behind summary: "I need the detail behind my A/P aging", "Show me line-level payables"
- Bills to pay: "What bills do I need to pay?", "Show me unpaid bills", "Any bills over $5K?", "Which bills are most overdue?" — pass transaction_type="bill" to filter to bills only
- Due-date windows: "Bills due this week", "What's due this month?", "Any bills due in the next 7 days?", "What bills are overdue?" — pass due_before with the appropriate cutoff date

DO NOT use this when:
- User asks for totals or high-level summaries by vendor → use qbo_accounting_get_ap_aging_summary
- User asks about receivables → use qbo_accounting_get_ar_aging_detail

PARAMETERS:
- as_of_date: The date to run the report as of (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today.
- vendor_name: Only show bills from vendors whose name contains this string (case-insensitive partial match).
  Use when the user mentions a specific vendor by name.
  Examples:
    "Show bills from Apple"             → vendor_name="Apple"
    "What do I owe Office Depot?"       → vendor_name="Office Depot"
- transaction_type: Filter by transaction type (currently only "bill" is supported). Case-insensitive. IMPORTANT: If the user's prompt mentions bills specifically — e.g. "bills", "unpaid bills", "bills to pay", "bills due this week" — you MUST pass transaction_type="bill" to filter to bills only. Omit this parameter when the user wants ALL A/P transaction types (which may include vendor credits and other entries).
- due_before: YYYY-MM-DD cutoff. Keep only bills due on or before this date (inclusive). IMPORTANT: When the user asks about a due-date window — e.g. "bills due this week", "due this month", "in the next N days", or "what's overdue?" — you MUST compute the appropriate cutoff date from today and pass it here. Examples (assume today is 2026-04-24):
    "Due this week"       → due_before="2026-04-25"   (upcoming end-of-week)
    "Due this month"      → due_before="2026-04-30"   (last day of current month)
    "Due in next 7 days"  → due_before="2026-05-01"   (today + 7 days)
    "Overdue bills"       → due_before="2026-04-23"   (yesterday — strictly before today)
  Omit this parameter when the user wants bills regardless of due date.
  NOTE: When due_before is a FUTURE date (after today), the tool automatically excludes already-overdue bills so upcoming-window queries return only the bills due within that window. For overdue views, pass yesterday's date — the tool will return all bills due on or before that date.

IMPORTANT: Before calling this tool, you MUST first call the 'company-info' tool to establish the QuickBooks connection.

AUTHENTICATION REQUIRED: You must authorize access to your QuickBooks account.

qbo_accounting_get_ap_aging_summary.description:
Get the A/P Aging Summary report from QuickBooks.

Shows TOTALS owed to each vendor grouped by aging buckets

IMPORTANT — DO NOT USE FOR GENERAL OVERDUE QUERIES: If the user asks "What's overdue?", "What's 60+ days overdue?", or similar questions WITHOUT explicitly mentioning bills, vendors, payables, or A/P, do NOT use this tool. Use qbo_accounting_get_ar_aging_summary instead. Only use THIS tool when the user explicitly mentions "bills", "vendors", "payables", "A/P", or "what I owe".

IMPORTANT: Before calling this tool, you MUST first call the 'company-info' tool to establish the QuickBooks connection. If 'company-info' has not been called yet in this conversation, call it first, then call this tool. This ensures the user is authenticated.

AUTHENTICATION REQUIRED: You must authorize access to your QuickBooks account.

Shows total sales grouped by product or service for a given period,
with quantity sold, average price, and percentage of total sales.

USE THIS when the user asks about:
- Product sales overview: "Show me sales by product", "What are my best selling items?", "Give me a product sales breakdown"
- Date-filtered sales: "Product sales for Q3", "What sold best in January?", "Product sales last month"
- Time-split trends: "Show me monthly product sales", "Quarterly product breakdown"
- Rankings: "Top 5 products by revenue", "Bottom sellers", "Which products contribute most?"
- Profitability: "What's my most profitable product?" (note: this tool shows REVENUE, not profit margin — clarify this to the user)
- Average price: "What's my average selling price by product?"
- Comparison: "How did [product] compare this year vs last year?", "Which products are growing?"

DO NOT use this when:
- User asks about customer-level sales → use qbo_accounting_get_sales_by_customer_summary
- User asks which products a SPECIFIC CUSTOMER bought → explain this tool shows product totals across all customers; suggest viewing the full report in QuickBooks
- User asks about product inventory or catalog → use qbo_accounting_get_product_service_list
- User asks about profit margins → this shows revenue only; suggest P&L report for cost data

PARAMETERS:
- date_range: Date macro. Defaults to THIS_YEAR. Common values:
    - "last year" → LAST_YEAR (previous calendar year)
    - "last 12 months" / "past year" → LAST_12_MONTHS (rolling 12 months from today)
    - "last month" → LAST_MONTH (previous calendar month)
    - "last 30 days" → LAST_30_DAYS (rolling 30 days)
    - "this year" / "year to date" / "YTD" → THIS_YEAR_TO_DATE
    - "this quarter" → THIS_QUARTER, "last quarter" → LAST_QUARTER
    Full list: TODAY, THIS_WEEK, THIS_WEEK_TO_DATE, LAST_WEEK, THIS_MONTH, THIS_MONTH_TO_DATE, LAST_MONTH, THIS_30_DAYS, LAST_30_DAYS, LAST_90_DAYS, LAST_6_MONTHS, LAST_12_MONTHS, THIS_QUARTER, THIS_QUARTER_TO_DATE, LAST_QUARTER, THIS_YEAR, THIS_YEAR_TO_DATE, LAST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR_TO_DATE, THIS_FISCAL_YEAR, THIS_FISCAL_YEAR_TO_DATE, LAST_FISCAL_YEAR, ALL.
- start_date / end_date: Custom date range (YYYY-MM-DD). Both must be provided together. Use for specific date requests like "sales from March 1 to March 15".
- accounting_method: "accrual" (default) or "cash".
- split_by: MONTH, QUARTER, YEAR, WEEK, or DAY. Use when the user asks for trends or time-based breakdown.
- product_name: Filter to products matching any name in the list (fuzzy match). Pass a list of strings. Examples: product_name=["consulting"] for consulting-related products, product_name=["consulting", "design"] for multiple. Use whenever the user mentions specific product names.
- value_filter_column / value_filter_op / value_filter_threshold: Filter rows by a numeric column value. All three MUST be provided together.
    - value_filter_column: "Amount", "Qty", "% of Sales", or "Avg Price"
    - value_filter_op: "gt", "gte", "lt", "lte", or "eq"
    - value_filter_threshold: numeric value
    Examples: "products with avg price above $5000" → value_filter_column="Avg Price", value_filter_op="gt", value_filter_threshold=5000
- top_n: Return only the top N products (descending by sort_by column, or Amount by default). Use for "top 5 products", "best sellers".
- bottom_n: Return only the bottom N products (ascending by sort_by column, or Amount by default). Use for "bottom sellers", "worst performing".
- sort_by: Sort rows descending by column. Valid values:
    - "Amount": total sales revenue
    - "Qty": quantity sold
    - "% of Sales": sales concentration
    - "Avg Price": average selling price

qbo_catalog_search_products.description:
PREFERRED tool for resolving products/services in invoice, estimate, and other sales flows. Use this — NOT qbo_accounting_get_product_service_list — whenever you need a product/service ID, price, or taxable flag for a line item. qbo_accounting_get_product_service_list is an accounting/reporting list tool: it does not return the fields required for sales line items, so do not call it when creating or editing invoices or estimates.

Search for products and services in QuickBooks Online by name (matching is performed against the product/service name, not the product description field). Provide up to 20 search strings to look up simultaneously. Returns matching product/service IDs, names, prices, and the taxable flag needed for invoice and estimate line items. If any item has found=false, call create_product immediately for each missing item. If any item has requires_clarification=true, show the candidates and ask the user which product they meant before proceeding.

qbo_sales_create_estimate.description:
Create a new estimate (quote) in QuickBooks Online. Requires a customer ID and at least one line item. Optionally set expiration date, discounts, and reference numbers. Returns the created estimate ID and a QuickBooks link. Pre-flight: search_customer then search_products. For each: if not found call create_*; if ambiguous ask user to pick before proceeding. After successfully creating the estimate, respond with ONE short sentence confirming the estimate was created (include customer name and total amount), then ONE sentence offering next steps. Do NOT list line items, financial breakdowns, or section headers. Format: "I've created an estimate for [customer] totaling [total]. [Open in QuickBooks]([link])

Ready to send, or make changes first? I can edit line items, pricing, or expiration date." Use the exact total and link from the tool result, including its currency symbol — do NOT add a "$" yourself. No headers, no bullet lists, no financial breakdowns.

Single-use links are tied to one customer and expire after one payment; multi-use links are reusable, no customer. Customer mentioned → single-use; none → ask which type. qbo_sales_create_recurring_invoice.description:
Create a recurring invoice template in QBO. Prefer over create_invoice for cadence wording (weekly/monthly/'every N months'/'recurring').

REQUIRED: customer_id, line_items. Default `name` to customer display_name from search_customer — do NOT ask.

DEFAULTS (omit unless asked): template_type=AUTOMATED; schedule → MONTHLY every 1mo day 1 alert=ALERT; runs forever; term_id, discount, shipping, addresses, tax_id, reference_number.

AUTOPAY & AUTO-SEND DEFAULT ON — pass online_payment.enable_cc/.enable_bank=true unless the user opts out. ALWAYS set email_delivery.to from the customer's search_customer `email` (not auto-filled; AutoPay consent needs it). No email: customer EXISTS → ask for one; just created → create anyway, report auto_send_reason. start_date today emails now — confirm first.

Report cadence, customer, lines, total, AutoPay, Auto-Send from the response; see autopay_reason/auto_send_reason when off. Close: "Here's your recurring invoice — review here: [<name>](<url>)." Use `url` verbatim.

qbo_sales_delete_estimate.description:
Delete an estimate (quote) in QuickBooks Online. Requires the estimate ID and confirmed=True.

BLOCKED (error MCP-0011): an estimate cannot be deleted when get_estimates returns accept_status.status of ACCEPTED, CONVERTED, or CLOSED, or when it has already been sent to the customer. Estimates with accept_status.status of PENDING or REJECTED (or none) that have not been sent are deletable.

Workflow:
(1) Call get_estimates to retrieve accept_status.status, customer name, total, currency_info, and reference number; show the amount with that currency symbol, never an assumed $.
(2) If blocked, refer the user to QuickBooks instead of calling this tool.
(3) Otherwise confirm: "Are you sure you want to delete Estimate [ref] for [Customer] for [Amount]? This cannot be undone."
(4) Only call with confirmed=True after the user confirms. The handler re-checks status and sent state and will still reject a blocked estimate.

qbo_sales_delete_invoice.description:
Delete an invoice in QuickBooks Online. Requires the invoice ID and confirmed=True.

BLOCKED (error MCP-0011): this tool checks the invoice internally and refuses to delete an invoice that has been sent (emailed or printed) or that has any amount paid against it (paid or partially paid). Draft, unsent, and unpaid invoices are deletable. You do not determine deletability yourself; if it is not deletable the tool returns MCP-0011 and you should tell the user to delete it manually in QuickBooks.

Workflow:
(1) Call get_invoices for the customer name, total and currency_info (it does not return a deletability status); show the amount with that currency symbol, never an assumed $.
(2) Confirm with the user: "Are you sure you want to delete this invoice for [Customer] for [Amount]? This cannot be undone."
(3) Only call this tool with confirmed=True after the user confirms; calling without it returns an error asking you to confirm first.
(4) If the tool returns MCP-0011, refer the user to the QuickBooks UI.

qbo_sales_delete_recurring_invoice.description:
Permanently delete a recurring invoice template from QBO by its template ID. Requires confirmed=True. Irreversible — template and schedule are removed; already-generated invoices are not affected.

Workflow:
(1) Resolve `template_id`. For a bare name like "cancel Westside Dental's recurring invoice", follow the bare-name lookup on `get_recurring_invoices`. Always disambiguate — never silently pick one before a delete.
(2) Call `get_recurring_invoices` with the `template_id` to fetch name, customer, schedule.
(3) Confirm with the user: "Delete recurring template '[Name]' for [Customer]? Cannot be undone; future occurrences stop."
(4) Call with confirmed=True only after the user confirms; otherwise returns CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED.
(5) Prefer `operate_recurring_invoice` with operation='pause' if the user only wants to stop future occurrences.

qbo_sales_get_estimates.description: Retrieve estimates (quotes) from QuickBooks Online. Filter by estimate IDs, doc numbers, date range, or customer ID. Returns estimate details including amounts, line items, customer info, expiry dates, and acceptance status. Defaults to last 180 days when no date range is given. Use estimate_ids when you have IDs from a prior tool result (guaranteed unique); use doc_numbers for user-visible filtering by estimate number. For bare numbers (e.g., "1001", "estimate 1001"): treat as DocNumber. Always try doc_numbers=["1001"] first, then retry with estimate_ids=["1001"] if empty. Partial failures are reported in meta.partial_failures — the call still returns success if at least one estimate is fetched. Example: "List all open estimates for ABC Corp from this quarter."

qbo_sales_get_invoices.description: Retrieve invoices from QuickBooks Online. Filter by invoice IDs, doc numbers, date range, or customer ID. Supports listing up to 1000 invoices with sorting. Returns invoice details including amounts, line items, customer info, due dates, and payment status. Defaults to last 180 days when no date range is given. Use invoice_ids when you have IDs from a prior tool result (guaranteed unique); use doc_numbers for user-visible filtering by invoice number. For bare numbers (e.g., "1001", "invoice 1001"): treat as DocNumber. Always try doc_numbers=["1001"] first, then retry with invoice_ids=["1001"] if empty. Partial failures are reported in meta.partial_failures — the call still returns success if at least one invoice is fetched. Example: "Show me all unpaid invoices from the last 60 days for Acme Corp."

qbo_sales_get_payment_links.description: Retrieve payment links (PaymentRequests) from QuickBooks Online. Requires payment_link_type ('single' or 'multi') — STS cannot return both types in one call. Optional filters: status (single value or a list for multi-status IN-matching), customer ID, creation date range (meta_created_after / meta_created_before) or exact day (meta_created_on). Returns payment link details including ID, amount, share URL, type, and status. Payment links are a QuickBooks Payments feature available to US and Canadian companies; elsewhere this returns an empty list with meta.note explaining why — relay the note and do not offer to create one.

qbo_sales_get_recurring_invoices.description:
Get recurring invoice templates from QBO. Two modes:
  - `template_id`: one template, full detail + `entity_version` (required by `update_recurring_invoice`; pre-check before delete/operate).
  - No `template_id`: list mode (template_type, template_name_filter, limit, offset). Mutually exclusive.
Each result has a `url` to show the user.

LIST MODE IS PARTIAL: only id, name, type, schedule (incl. AutoPay). `entity_version`, `header` (customer, amount), `traits` (Auto-Send, payment methods) and `line_items` are null = NOT returned, not empty/$0/off. Fetch by `template_id` before answering about them.

BARE-NAME LOOKUP ("Acme's recurring invoice") — token may be a template label OR customer name. In order:
  1. `template_name_filter="<token>"`. One hit → use it; several → ask.
  2. Zero hits (or wrong customer) → `search_customer` → list unfiltered → fetch each by `template_id`, match `header.contact.id`. Ask if >1.
  3. Still nothing → tell the user.
Don't skip step 1 because the token looks like a name.

qbo_sales_get_settings.description: Read sales domain settings from a QuickBooks Online merchant account. Also get_global: tips, late_fees, deposits, discount, service_date, custom_txn_numbers, progress_invoicing, imported_invoices (auto-send), classes (on/off + per-txn vs per-line), locations (on/off + label).

qbo_sales_operate_recurring_invoice.description:
Pause/resume/skip-next a recurring invoice template. skip_next requires confirm=true and schedule.active=true (if paused, resume first).

INTENT MAPPING:
- "pause for N months/until <date>" → "pause". QBO has no pause_until — compute today+N, tell user to resume manually. NOT update_recurring_invoice end_date (that TERMINATES).
- "resume [now]" → "resume". No run-template-now action exists; do NOT ask about generating an invoice immediately.
- "skip next cycle/month" → "skip_next" (acts on schedule, not an existing invoice — not delete_invoice; not pause).

AFTER SUCCESS — this response omits schedule/next_date/customer/lines. ALWAYS call get_recurring_invoices (single mode) first, then report nextDate / active state from it, never as null from here.

ID RESOLUTION: never ask the user to confirm the label first. Call get_recurring_invoices with template_name_filter="<name>". 1 hit → use silently; 0 → follow that tool's bare-name chain; ≥2 → ask, quoting candidates. Never pass a name as template_id.

qbo_sales_send_invoice_reminder.description:
Send QBO payment reminders.
STOP: call only after the user says yes to 'Send these reminders?' for the exact list last shown. Answering another question (scope, count) is not a yes, nor is your own 'sending now'.
1. BUILD THE LIST with qbo_sales_get_invoices, the only source of invoice ids. NEVER use qbo_accounting_get_ar_aging_* to build or re-check it; use the report shown for totals. After a reminder request, later narrowing ('most overdue for Acme') is still building it. Customer name: qbo_contact_search_customer for customer_id; invoice number: doc_numbers.
transaction_date, first that applies: (a) the period the user named. (b) An AR aging report in the conversation: cover its open invoices — to_date = its as_of_date (today if unset), from_date wide. Below the report's total? Widen and retry; if the call errors, narrow and report the gap. (c) Otherwise a wide range.
No payment_status field: overdue = balance_amount > 0 and due_date past.
2. POST THE DRAFT, ask 'Send these reminders?', and end your turn. In plain words, not parameter names, say what each search covered: dates, max results, customer, invoice numbers, sort. If a call hit max results, say the list may be cut off. Report what your search found, never what QuickBooks has; beside an AR report, show both totals. List every invoice: ref#, customer, balance, email; if too many, ask to narrow. When the user narrows or changes the list, your next reply IS the new draft — never just acknowledge or announce a next step. Once, quote the subject AND full body verbatim: your custom_subject/custom_message (one invoice only), else the template from qbo_sales_get_settings {domain:'reminder_template',action:'get_global'}; never summarize it.
3. SEND after they reply yes. On failure say so and stop; NEVER fall back to qbo_sales_send_invoice (it mails the invoice, not a reminder).
Holds (MCP-0020/0021/0023): nothing is sent; the error message is your instruction. emails={invoice_id:address} also overrides on-file.

A real id is a long numeric string (15+ digits); never type a short, rounded, or guessed number from memory — copy the exact id string the tool returned, or call get_payment_links first if you do not have it. Only call after the user has explicitly confirmed they want to send the link. Never call this automatically after create_payment_link — always wait for explicit user confirmation first. Only works for single-use links — multi-use/reusable links are always rejected; share share_link directly instead. Payment links exist only for US and Canadian companies (QuickBooks Payments); elsewhere this returns an error — relay it, do not retry.

Flow: 1. Clarify link type (single-use or multi-use). 2. Find the link — id from context, else call qbo_sales_get_payment_links. 3. Confirm the correct link with the user. 4. Ask what to change. 5. If clear from context, call the tool — confirm only if changes are ambiguous. payment_link_id must be the opaque id, never share_link or a derived value. INITIAL status: update without sending, then ask whether to send. SENT/VIEWED/UNDELIVERED: re-send automatically unless the user says no. After update show: customer, amount, description, link, and one line of changes. share_link as a markdown hyperlink, no raw URLs. Display any warning.

Update a recurring invoice template in QBO. Change name, type, schedule, customer, lines, discount, addresses, shipping, tax, online-payment, email_send (Auto-Send on/off), or payment instructions. Omitted fields carry forward.

Requires template_id + entity_version. Missing either → get_recurring_invoices (list for id, single-mode for version — don't reuse list's null version).

Only re-fetch if a field is missing. Close: "Here's your updated recurring invoice — review the template here: [<name>](<url>). Let me know if you'd like to change any details." Use `url` verbatim.
